correctness.rationale: Sign averaging preserves upper/lower quadratic comparison for all real x,y and removes cross terms. For q>2 write m=q/2>1,t=y²: F_r(t)=1-t^m+rt. Its minimum is min(1,r); for 0<r<m the maximum is 1+(m-1)(r/m)^[m/(m-1)] and for r≥m it is r. On r≤1, r² D'(r)=-1+(r/m)^[m/(m-1)]<0; for r≥1 the numerator grows or D=r. The unique ratio minimum is r=1, giving d_BM²=1+(m-1)m^[-m/(m-1)]. q=4 yields 5/4. This is an all-real-q proof, not numerical extrapolation.
